# Orbit feature checklist

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/features.mjs` from the behaviour spec, the tests and docs/feature-status.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every row is one behaviour from the clean-room spec. Status per ID: **spec’d** (every row) → **built** → **tested** (a unit or e2e test names the ID) → **feels right** (lead sign-off after a hands-on review against `feel.md`).

**Totals:** 472 spec’d · 324 built (58 partial) · 388 tested · 202 feel right. 13 more are out of scope and not counted.

| Priority | Spec’d | Built | Tested |
|---|---|---|---|
| P0 | 174 | 161 | 173 |
| P1 | 219 | 143 | 189 |
| P2 | 79 | 20 | 26 |

P0 = milestone-1 core experience, P1 = parity, P2 = later.

While a Peek is open the row menu is the system's: the Peek has the overlay then, and the sidebar must not close it (PK-13) |

| TB-17 | Tabs across multiple windows | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | tab handoff; no two windows ever show the same tab (close, Clear, archive, moves, undo, drag-out); New Blank Window (⌃⌘N on macOS, remappable; the command bar everywhere) and a tab dragged out of the sidebar open a blank window in the profile of the window it came from: its own sidebar, starting empty (or with the dragged tab, which ⌘Z puts back; a pinned tab, Favorite or split pane goes as a copy), out of the Space list, with no Spaces, pinned tabs, Favorites or folders; no other window lists or finds its tabs, and it finds only its own; open at quit, it comes back after a relaunch; closed, or missing at load (a crash part-way through closing it), its tabs go to the Archive; a link its page opens in a new window (⇧-click when Peek doesn't take it, the page menu's Open Link in New Window, the page's own request) opens in a new blank window of its profile (D88) |

## Page navigation, windows, links and page-level controls (prefix NV)

Spec: `spec/navigation.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| NV-01 | Back and forward | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | buttons and keys (Cmd+Left/Right only outside text fields), history menu with favicons that closes on tab switch, Cmd/middle-click opens the entry in a background tab with its history; mouse side buttons are Chromium's; Backspace inert |
| NV-02 | Trackpad two-finger swipe back/forward | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | a horizontal two-finger swipe over the page goes back or forward: an arrow slides in from that edge of the page's card, following the fingers 1:1, fills once it's fully in (112 px), and letting go then goes as Back and Forward do; let go sooner, it fades and nothing happens. Only with somewhere to go, and on macOS only with the system's Swipe between pages on. The page gets the swipe first: while what's under the pointer (or around it) can still scroll that way, or the page uses the wheel (preventDefault), the swipe is the page's until the fingers lift, so it navigates only at the scroll edge. Over the sidebar the same swipe switches Space (SP-08) and never navigates. Not offered over a Peek's, a Mini Window's or a pop-up's page, where the swipe does nothing (the spec doesn't say). Windows and Linux: wherever the touchpad scrolls smoothly (pixel deltas); a mouse wheel's notches never navigate. Recognition follows the Space swipe (FL-13): 9 px decide the axis, and the fingers have lifted after a 90 ms pause or when the OS momentum starts. Limits: Electron reports no scroll phases, so the page preload watches the page's wheel events in its own world (D40 use orbit-page:swipe); the swipe goes by the scroll's direction, so with macOS's natural scrolling off a swipe right is forward; a swipe that starts over a frame of the page stays the frame's (frames get no preload); the arrow's small view takes the wheel if the pointer is right over it. Tests use synthetic trackpad scrolls; the real gesture, with momentum, is unverified on macOS (person-check) |
| NV-03 | Reload and hard reload | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | Cmd/Ctrl+R, F5; hard reload Cmd+Shift+R, Ctrl+Shift+R, Shift+F5, Ctrl+F5; Cmd/middle-click Reload duplicates with history; keyboard focus goes to the page |
| NV-04 | Stop loading | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | Esc in the page while loading (overlays take it first; a page that uses Esc keeps it and goes on loading, D59), Cmd+. on macOS, double-click Reload, Stop (x) state; a typed address, Back/Forward or Reload shows where it is going at once and stays when stopped; the loading indicator goes. Known limit (keys fix check K6): a page's answer about an Esc that comes after Orbit stopped waiting for it (250 ms) answers the next Esc pressed while that page loads |
| NV-05 | Find in page | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | floating bar over the active page's top-right corner; finds as you type, n/m count, No matches; Enter/Cmd+G/F3 next, Shift+Enter/Shift+Cmd+G/Shift+F3 previous, buttons; Esc closes and keeps the match selected; per tab (hidden on switch, back with text and place); starts from the selection, else the last search; IME commits; keys typed for the bar before it has the keyboard (a new window's first moments, a busy bar) wait up to 5 s and then go into it in order, text as text (any character on the keyboard's own layout); it takes the keyboard when it shows, even later than that; shortcuts and IME composition are not held; Cmd+J jumps to the selection (macOS); Edit > Find menu; with a Peek open the bar finds in the Peek, over its card (PK-11); a Mini Window finds with a field in its top bar (MW-03). Known limits (chrome fix check 4, N3, by reading): keys held while a replay of held keys runs past 5 s (each held Backspace, Enter or Escape waits up to 1 s for the bar) are dropped, and keys typed after that can reach the bar ahead of the rest of the replay; keys held after a held Escape are dropped, where a ready bar would have let them reach the page once it closed; and a held character an auto-type tool maps onto the keyboard on the fly, which Chromium names "\u0000", is lost (chrome fix check 4) |

In full screen the sidebar hides and the page fills the window; the window's left edge brings the sidebar in over the page (SB-12), and the loading indicator stays (SB-28). Leaving docks the sidebar again, unless the user docked or hid it meanwhile (⌘S); a window closed or quit in full screen keeps its docked sidebar for next time; a window opened from one in full screen opens in full screen, its sidebar hidden (NV-10). Esc in a page, or over its error or crash screen, goes to the page first and full screen stays; pressed again within a second, or held (at its first repeat), it leaves full screen, and the page gets neither that press nor its repeats (nor, as the engine does after a key it didn't deliver, the release); presses further apart each go to the page. A single Esc never leaves, even one the page left alone: nothing asks the page (D60), and a web app's Esc is often its own without preventDefault. Exit Full Screen in Settings → Shortcuts prefers websites by default; set to prefer Orbit, one Esc leaves at once and the page gets nothing of it (KS-02, D68). Esc is no binding of it: an open overlay (command bar, Peek, find bar, a page dialog) takes Esc first (KS-19). The Esc that leaves full screen on a loading page doesn't stop the load (NV-04). A video's own full screen is Chromium's: it fills the window without the sidebar, Esc leaves only it, and the toggle keys leave both. Mini Windows don't go full screen this way. Xvfb has no window manager, so the e2e tests check the state and layout Orbit keeps; a person checks that the window really fills the screen, the macOS animation (the sidebar goes and comes back as it ends), fn+F / Globe+F, and that the View menu has one full-screen item (macOS may add its own Enter Full Screen beside Orbit's). Known limits (keys lane): with the keyboard in a frame of a loading page, the Esc the page gets stops the load after 250 ms, as only the main frame answers (K5); the first key right after the keyboard moves into a frame can come before that frame says where its keyboard is (K7) |

The OS save dialog opens from the Downloads folder, named after the page: a web page saves as a single file (MHTML) or, named .html, as its HTML alone; a local page whose frames are all local files saves complete (D49). A Peek's or a Mini Window's page saves itself. View Source is DT-04. On a canvas tab the same command exports the canvas: that comes with EZ-11 (no canvases yet). |

("Reload site?" for a reload) when a page that asks for it, from its main frame or a frame (one from another site too), after a user gesture in any of its frames as in Chromium (a click, or a key that reaches the page, a shortcut that goes to the page first included, such as Ctrl+S and Ctrl+Shift+C on Windows and Linux by default; a shortcut Orbit takes first is none, so ⌘W is none unless it is set to go to websites first, D77), goes: a link, a form or location, Orbit's address, Back, Forward or Reload (Leave starts it again), closing its tab (shown first; The OS window is not resized, which would lay the page out every frame: the page's native view, loading all along, sits out the grow and joins on the card at full size when it ends. Reduced motion shows it at once. The ready window Orbit keeps hidden draws itself empty until it opens, because a window shows the frame it drew last first: a link opens with its page's bar, never the blank lookup bar, and a blank window first shows early in its grow, not at full size. Opens at the last-used size and place, each further window 24 px down and right; on macOS it shows above a full-screen Orbit window, on the current desktop. Only a person can check the desktop and full-screen parts, on a Mac |
| MW-05 | Move the page into a Space ("Open in…") | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | ⌘O to the most recent Space, Open in… / ⌘⌥O (⌘⇧O) native Space menu; live page, no reload |
| MW-06 | Open a blank Mini Window for a quick lookup | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | ⌘⌥N opens a pre-rendered blank window with a focused lookup bar, the command bar's compact variant (CB-23): history and typed-text rows, inline completion, site search, engine suggestions; the choice loads here; Esc empties it, Esc on the empty bar or ⌘W closes the window. System-wide on macOS only (outside e2e); on Windows/Linux Ctrl+Alt+N works inside Orbit, so other apps (and AltGr+N) keep the key |
| MW-07 | Open a link or a tab in a Mini Window on purpose | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | ⌘⌥-click a link, link menu Open Link in Mini Window, or ⌘⌥-click a sidebar row: Today rows move live, pinned/Favorite rows open a copy |
| MW-08 | Several Mini Windows at once | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | any number; Show/Hide All action and macOS dock menu |
| MW-09 | Closing, auto-archive and the Archive | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | close and idle auto-close (settings.miniWindowArchiveAfterMs, 6 h, 0 = never; not while audible) archive with from 'mini' |
| MW-10 | Profiles | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | profile pill/menu reopens the page in another profile; remembered per site |
| MW-11 | Turning the Mini Window off | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | settings.miniWindowForExternalLinks off: tabs in the most recent or chosen Space (externalLinksSpace) |
| MW-12 | What works inside a Mini Window | P2 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | a video's full screen happens in the Mini Window: the window fills the screen with the page, which stays there, and the card comes back on exit (tested); copy URL, devtools, downloads through the profile's session. Not built: extensions (Orbit has no extension support yet, EX-11), captures saved to a canvas (no Canvases yet) and sharing (Orbit has no share feature) |
| MW-13 | Menu-bar / tray button | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | off by default; Settings > General > Mini Window turns it on: Orbit's mark as a template glyph in the macOS menu bar, the app's icon in the Windows and Linux tray (the drawn mark where a build has no icon file); a click opens a blank Mini Window with its lookup bar focused (macOS: right-click for its menu); its menu has New Mini Window and Show/Hide All Mini Windows, New Mini Window first for Linux trays that show only the menu (tested through the button's click and menu). GNOME shows tray icons only with an AppIndicator extension; on Windows and Linux Orbit still quits with its last window, button or not |
| MW-14 | Platforms | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | all platforms with Ctrl+Alt+N / Ctrl+O / Ctrl+Alt+O, in-app outside macOS (D23), with the tray button (MW-13) as the way in from other apps; New Mini Window and Show/Hide All in the macOS dock menu, the Windows jump list, Linux launcher actions and the tray menu. Launcher actions: a packaged Linux folder build writes ~/.local/share/applications/<name>.desktop at start-up (under $XDG_DATA_HOME when that is set; <name> is Electron's desktop name), with no opt-out for now, and keeps it pointing at where Orbit runs from. It never touches an entry a package installed, one the user wrote, or one it can't read (checked on a packaged build: both actions reach the running Orbit). Only a person can check the Windows jump list |
| MW-15 | Feel | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | warm spare window takes keys at once, page loads before the window shows; opens with MW-04's 200 ms grow and fade; Open in… shrinks to 92% and fades (140 ms, macOS/Windows) as the row enters Today; closing and Open in… never leave the window on screen without its page or UI: where the window fades out its card shows a still of the page as the page leaves, if one is taken within 150 ms (macOS, Windows; not run here), elsewhere the window leaves the screen first, whole |

## Picture-in-picture, sidebar media player and call controls (prefix MD)

Spec: `spec/media.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| MD-01 | Automatic picture-in-picture when leaving a video tab | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Orbit's own floating player: leaving a tab whose main video plays (tab, Space or split change; the largest playing video, in the page or in any of its frames, cross-site ones included) moves it there within ~300 ms, still playing; not when paused, muted or turned off (MD-08); selecting the tab again puts it back in the page (or its frame) with no blank video frame, at any load (a frame's page does it from its own size, before its first frame back is drawn), and its view waits out of sight, at its pane's size, until the page has drawn there, then moves in. Whichever way it comes back (selected, Back to tab, ⌘W on the tab over it, or from an empty Space, alone or in a split), the player hides first (Back to tab flies a still of it back to the page, MD-16), and no frame of its player layout reaches the page area if the page draws within 250 ms; a page slower than that shows what it drew last. Until the page has drawn, the page area keeps the page it showed, which takes clicks (selected, Back to tab), or shows the pane's blank card in its Space's colour (⌘W on the tab over it, or from an empty Space, alone or in a split; FL-29 allows a placeholder in the page's background): 6–9 frames for a page 150 ms slow to lay out. Meanwhile the held view keeps one pixel inside the window, so that it draws: the window's bottom-right pixel shows the page's top-left one, for 8–11 frames on Linux (whether rounded window corners hide it on macOS is unchecked). Moving between a split's panes doesn't float it, nor does a Peek's video when its Peek goes. A frame inside a shadow tree can't be found from its page: its video plays on in the tab and in the sidebar controller instead. Known limit (D71): a page's own picture-in-picture button inside a frame returns to the tab without raising the window; the tab is selected only when its window already has focus, in the Space it shows, and once for each frame document (D74). Known limit (D74): a page can end its own picture-in-picture once with exitPictureInPicture() and bring the window forward, as the engine's Back to tab button does; moving it to another of its videos brings nothing forward. Known limit (D78): while a frame's video is in the player, the frame's page can see a hidden div the size of its viewport under <html>, which the frame's script watches, with the root element, to put the video back before the frame is drawn; when the frame's own script, not main, puts a same-site frame's video back, the page may get one "ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications" error event, and then its own observers of <html> or <body> get the final size a frame later, as they did before |
| MD-02 | Open picture-in-picture manually | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | Picture in Picture in a video's page right-click menu, the Picture in Picture action and the tray's PiP button; while the tab stays selected the engine's own PiP window shows the video (Orbit's player needs the tab's view), so its controls are the engine's until the tab is left and Orbit's player takes over |
| MD-03 | The floating player's look and placement | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | frameless, always-on-top window, 320x180 for 16:9 (keeps the video's shape), bottom-right 16 px inside the work area; rounded corners (a window shape where the system has none) and shadow; video only until hovered, then controls over a dark gradient; the same player on every platform |
| MD-04 | Floating player controls | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | on hover: play/pause, +/-15 s, progress with elapsed and total time (seekable; LIVE badge for streams), Back to tab (selects it in its window and Space), x (keeps playing in the sidebar), ... menu (playback speed, turn off today / always for the site), previous/next for Media Session pages; double-click goes back to the tab |
| MD-05 | Keyboard and media keys for the floating player | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | with the player focused (clicked) Space plays and pauses and the arrow keys seek 5 s, its buttons 15 s (tested); hardware media keys reach the playing video through Chromium's media key handling, which Orbit turns on: only a person can check them (no media keys under Xvfb) |
| MD-06 | Move, resize and zoom the floating player | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | drag or two-finger hover-scroll moves it and it glides to the corner the release or fling heads for; corner drag resizes keeping the shape, at least 200 px wide (tall videos too) and at most half the screen width and the screen's height, with rubber-band resistance; Cmd/Ctrl+scroll or pinch zooms (crops) inside the window; corner and size remembered. While an Orbit window shows an alert or dialog (the engine disables the window meanwhile, macOS shows a sheet, and Orbit's own file pickers and save dialogs say so; so do Orbit's dialogs and screens over a page while they show: a page's alert, confirm, prompt and "Open Mail?", the print dialog, and the error, crash and "Page unresponsive" screens), the player keeps clear of where it shows, up to 900 x 620 centered on the window (from its top on macOS): it glides to the nearest clear corner at its size, or goes out of sight, still playing, when no corner is clear, and comes back when the dialog closes unless it was moved meanwhile; its remembered place doesn't change (tested with an alert, and with a page's confirm, the print dialog and a crash screen). A web page's own file picker on Linux isn't seen: the engine doesn't disable the window for it |
| MD-07 | Ending picture-in-picture | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | returning (select, double-click, Back to tab) ends it with the video playing in the page; x closes it and the media keeps playing in the sidebar controls; closing or unloading the tab stops media and player; navigating the tab or the video ending closes it, without replay; a picture-in-picture the engine closes because another one opened (in another pane, tab or window, by a page or by Orbit) isn't Back to tab: nothing is selected and no window comes forward (D75) |
| MD-08 | Turning automatic picture-in-picture off | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | site controls panel (NV-16) Picture in Picture switch, on by default: off is Always turn off for this site, on undoes it and Turn off for today, which it shows too; player ... menu Turn Off for Today / Always Turn Off for This Site (also in the tray controller menu); global switch Settings > Advanced (ST-10) and the Picture in Picture action; turning off keeps playback (sidebar controls); muted tabs never trigger |
| MD-09 | Sidebar media controls for background audio | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | controller above the bottom bar: the Media Session's artwork (loaded with the tab's session, kept small) or the favicon, Media Session title/artist or tab title (marquee), play/pause, next, previous where supported, x pauses and hides; click jumps to the tab (switching Space); quiet audio counts; hidden while its tab is selected; media in frames (embedded players, cross-site too) has the same controls |
| MD-10 | Several players: the media tray | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | one controller per background tab, newest first, appears and disappears by itself, works across windows; a video's controller has Picture in Picture (Back to PiP): the player grows out of the controller while the controller gives way |
| MD-11 | Audio and recording indicators, mute | P0 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | pulsing camera/microphone indicator on tab rows (tracks the page shows); a distinct blue screen-share indicator, lit while either source says a share is live (D69): main's watcher, put in the asking frame (any frame) when Orbit's screen chooser grants, or the page preload's count of the main frame's live shared tracks (covers macOS 15's system picker); only chooser grants keep a tab awake and unarchived; known limit: a page that wants to hide its share can (e.g. clone a track with a same-origin frame's built-ins and stop the one Orbit follows), the OS's own indicator is the backstop; a frame's share the macOS 15 picker grants doesn't show; a capture that fails after the chooser granted it shows until the page leaves; Peek and Mini Window shares have no row; per-pane Mute/Unmute in the split row's menu (split lane's menu, tested here: only that pane goes silent); the recent-tab switcher (TB-05) shows the same camera/microphone and screen-share indicators, and the sound state, as the rows |
| MD-12 | Media and the tab lifecycle | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | playing (muted too), PiP and camera/mic tabs never sleep, auto-archive, Clear or Archive Below; closing stops media, PiP and controller; isAnyMediaPlaying() is ready for the updates lane |
| MD-13 | Video calls: automatic call picture-in-picture | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | leaving a call tab floats the largest participant video (never the self view) in Orbit's player with microphone/camera toggles and Back to call tab; moves and resizes like any video (a pinch zooms, as for any video). Not built: leave call (the site's Media Session hang-up handler lives in the page's own script world, which Orbit reaches only through a page patch, a lead decision under D40), a chat toggle (no web API exposes a site's chat), and the site's own document picture-in-picture view (also only through the page's Media Session) |
| MD-14 | Call controls in the sidebar | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | a background call tab (or a closed call window) gets a sidebar call controller: microphone and camera toggles (track.enabled on the tracks the page shows) and jump back. Not built: a call is seen only when its page shows its own camera (a self view); an audio-only call isn't, because the browser process can't see what a page captures and watching getUserMedia takes a page patch (a lead decision under D40) |
| MD-15 | Switch which tab is being screen-shared | P2 | – | – | – | not possible as specified: Orbit's screen chooser shares a screen or a window, never a single tab, and the engine can't change what a running share captures (switching the shared tab is the Chrome browser's own feature, not in Electron); swapping the call page's video track would take a page patch, a lead decision under D40 |
| MD-16 | Feel: entering and leaving picture-in-picture | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | enter: the video shrinks from its place in the page to the corner (~300 ms, standard curve); Back to tab/double-click: the tab is selected at once, and the player's window, showing a still of the last frame, flies to the video's place in the page (220 ms, over the window: always on top) and hides; under Xvfb, with no window manager, the selected window comes over the player, so the flight can't be seen there; release glides to the corner; Back to PiP grows from the controller; tray slides with the snappy spring; with reduced motion (FL-28) the player appears and goes without motion and a release settles with a 120 ms ease-out. Not possible: a haptic tick on macOS (Electron has no haptics; it would take native code), and fading in the engine's own PiP window, which shows only while the tab stays selected (MD-02). Only a person can check playback for stutter |

## Archive, recently closed, history and sidebar backups (prefix AR)

Spec: `spec/archive.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| AR-01 | What goes into the Archive | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | close, auto-archive, Clear, archive-below, pinned/folder/Space delete, Mini Window and Peek pages; entries carry tab, Space name, section, reason; back/forward history kept outside OrbitState (userData/archive, page state in memory only); private and empty tabs never archived; state keeps the newest ~200-300, the rest lives in the Archive store |
| AR-02 | Where the Archive lives and how to open it | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | Library view over the page area (its own view above the tabs, below the command bar and Peek) from the bottom-bar button, ⌘⇧L (Open Library), ⌘T View Archive / Open Library and the macOS Archive menu; reopens to the last section; Esc, ⌘W or selecting another tab closes it and the page gets the keys back; section registry (*.library-section.tsx) for other lanes; closed, or made ahead of its first open, it draws nothing, so no half-drawn Library shows before it fades in, and only the section it opens on is marked; closing, its view leaves the window once it has drawn itself faded out (500 ms at the latest) |
| AR-03 | Archive list layout | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | newest first under Today / Yesterday / date headings; favicon, title, host, time and origin-Space badge; filters by source (all, sidebar, Mini Window), Space and how it closed; per profile (PR-05); virtualised and paged, fast at 10k entries. A row click previews (AR-06); ⌘-click and ⇧-click select |
| AR-04 | Search the Archive | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | search field filters on each keystroke (title and URL, case-insensitive, partial words, every word) using the Archive store's keys (history queryTerms/urlKeyOf); typing on narrows the last answer; Enter restores and shows the top or highlighted match; ⌘F focuses it. The command bar's Archived results search the whole Archive store of the profile, not only the recent entries kept in state |
| AR-05 | Restore an archived tab | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | Restore (hover button, Enter, row menu, several selected) puts tabs at the top of their Space's Today in order, with their tab id and back/forward history when the profile matches (never across profiles); routing rule > origin Space > current Space; toast with Go to Space when it lands elsewhere; command bar restores without a jump. A row click previews (AR-06) instead of restoring. Undoing Delete Folder after the Space changed profile also follows the new profile (W3) |
| AR-06 | Preview an archived item without restoring | P2 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | a row click opens its page in a Peek over the Library (the Peek component, its open and close motion); the entry stays archived. ⌘W and Esc close only the Peek and the Library takes the keys back (Enter then restores that row); Open as Tab (⌘O) opens it as a tab and keeps the entry; closing a preview, or a reopen of it, archives no second entry. Missing: a Restore button in the Peek card (peek lane). The Peek carries overlay.archiveEntry and archive.restorePreview restores and closes it. With no tab to preview over (an empty Space), a click opens the page in a new tab |
| AR-07 | Clear the Archive | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | Clear Archive… from the Archive entry’s right-click menu in the Library, Archive → Clear Archive… (macOS app menu) and the command bar; always asks in the Library first (Cancel has the focus, Esc cancels), says it can’t be undone and that browsing history is kept; clears the profile shown, and the cleared pages leave the disk at once (the log is rewritten). Delete (a row’s menu, or Delete for the selected rows) shows a toast whose Undo puts the entries back with their history for a minute |
| AR-08 | Retention of archived entries | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | settings.archiveKeepDays, default 30; 30 Days / 90 Days / 1 Year / Forever from the Archive entry’s menu in the Library and Archive → Keep Archived Tabs For (macOS) until Settings exist. A shorter time that would delete entries asks first, in the Library, saying how many (Cancel keeps them all and the time as it was). Purged once the Archive is read at launch, hourly, and at once when a shorter time is confirmed; browsing history is not touched |
| AR-09 | Reopen recently closed tabs | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | ⌘⇧T and ⌘Z walk back through closes with full history (TB-07, TB-18); ⌘Z also shows the tab again when it was the one shown; a closed Peek comes back through the same key (PK-10, peek lane). A page closed in the last 10 minutes keeps its history rank in the command bar (as the archived row). macOS File menu: Reopen Closed Tab and a Recently Closed submenu of the last 10; on every platform the Archive toolbar has a Recently Closed menu. Neither list shows a tab of a private or deleted profile |
| AR-10 | Browsing history view | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | History is a page in a tab, as D39 planned once internal pages existed: orbit://history/ shows every visit of the tab's profile from the history store, newest first by day, virtualised and paged, with search (all words, title or address). ⌘Y (Ctrl+H), Archive → View History (macOS) and the command bar's View History show the History tab of the Space the window shows (the one used last), else open one; an open Library makes way; from a Mini Window it shows in the latest main window. The list loads again each time its tab shows again. A row opens its page in a new tab (⌘-click or middle-click: behind); its × or its menu (Open in New Tab, Open in Background, Copy Link, Remove from History) removes every visit to the page. The page asks main only about its own tab's profile and opens only pages it listed (D53). The Library keeps its History section, the same list. Clearing the Archive leaves history alone |
| AR-11 | Sidebar backups and "Restore Data" | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Backups of the whole sidebar (Spaces, each profile’s Favorites, pinned and Today tabs, folders, split views; no private profiles) in userData/backups, one JSON file each: taken within 5 minutes of a sidebar change (only when it differs from the newest; browsing alone never makes one), once 30 s after launch, before every restore, and with Back Up Now. Kept: the newest 10 of today, then the newest of each of the 10 days before, of each week of the month before that and of each 30 days of the year before that; a deleted profile’s Favorites, Spaces and tabs are taken out of every backup. Help → Restore Data… (macOS) and the command bar open the Backups section of the Library: a dated list (day headings, time, Spaces and tabs; a file that can’t be read is listed as such, without Restore); Restore… asks first, then puts the sidebar back: tabs in both keep their page, tabs only in the backup come back asleep (with the page and history the Archive kept for them, leaving the Archive), tabs opened since go to the Archive, Spaces added since go; private windows and their tabs are left alone; Favorites over 12 go to Today (D33). When the sidebar can’t be backed up first, nothing changes. A running import stops first: none of the tabs it hasn’t shown yet go to the Archive, and its window says why (D65). Each restore is one step on the sidebar’s undo stack (TB-18): the toast’s Undo or ⌘Z, also in the Library, puts back the sidebar it replaced, a second ⌘Z goes further back and ⌘⇧Z restores again; earlier steps stay. After an undo, a window moved off a removed Space stays where it went, and the pages come back asleep. A folder that comes back with its tabs draws its row in the frame they first show, above them |

Spec: `spec/shortcuts.md`

| KS-03 | Platform mapping rules | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | every default checked against the spec tables on macOS, Windows and Linux (unit test): ⌘ → Ctrl, ⌥ → Alt, ⌃ keys (⌃Tab, the split keys) stay Ctrl; the Windows/Linux exceptions Alt+1–9 for Spaces, Ctrl+H, Alt+←/→, Alt+D, F5, F3, Ctrl+F4 and F1; Alt+F4 and Alt+F are kept for the system; a Ctrl+Alt key that typed an AltGr character acts only outside text fields; letters and symbols follow the layout; F11 and Alt+Shift+F for full screen (NV-20); keys the system keeps are marked in Settings → Shortcuts, which says where to turn them off: macOS Mission Control “Switch to Desktop N” (⌃1–⌃9 when turned on) and, on Linux, the desktop's own keys (GNOME's, Cinnamon's and MATE's window manager and system keys, Xfce's and KDE Plasma's global shortcuts; the workspace keys and Alt+F-keys among them; desktops that keep theirs in a config file of their own, such as sway or i3, report none). Linux first run: onboarding has a Shortcuts step when the desktop keeps keys Orbit's actions are bound to, each with a free key to use instead (the same keys with Shift where free; never a key that edits text or one desktops often keep); nothing changes until the user takes them (all, or the ones left ticked); Keep them changes nothing; Choose other keys opens Settings → Shortcuts at the action; it shows once, as onboarding does. Mini Window: ⌘W closes it, ⌘O / ⌘⌥O move or offer to move its page (KS-10), ⌘L edits its address with the keyboard in the field and Esc gives the keyboard back to its page, ⌘R, zoom and print act on its page, sidebar and Space keys do nothing; ⌘Y / Ctrl+H History, the Library and Help → Keyboard Shortcuts open in the browser window behind it; keys given to Tweak actions act from it too (BO-21): View Tweaks opens the Library there, and the others say there why its page takes no Tweak. ## Interaction feel and motion targets (prefix FL)

Spec: `spec/feel.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FL-01 | Motion principles and shared tokens | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | one token set in shared/motion.ts and motion.css (instant 90 ms, quick 130 ms, pop 240 ms; snappy, standard and pop springs), checked against each other by a unit test; interrupted motions turn round from where they are (Space slide, command bar, hover card, folders, ⌘S), checked as speeds from the first frame that shows the input handled |
| FL-02 | Sidebar show/hide (docked toggle) | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | 260 ms standard curve drives the sidebar column and the card margins together; interruptible; reduced motion snaps; starts a frame along, so the frame that draws ⌘S already moves |
| FL-03 | Sidebar hover-reveal overlay | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | 0 ms dwell; card in 200 ms (snappy), out 160 ms (quick); hysteresis band; re-entering while it leaves brings it back |
| FL-04 | Tab row hover | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | row hover lights on the instant timing and fades out from where it is when the pointer leaves; every row a sweep enters lights |
| FL-05 | Tab selection | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | a press selects the row in its frame, before the page shows (within 50 ms); a press on a row still growing in selects it; a selected row out of sight scrolls into view with a 225 ms ease-out, or at once from more than two screens away or with reduced motion |
| FL-06 | New-tab insertion | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | a new row grows with the snappy spring, its content fading in over the last 60 %; the rows below glide |
| FL-07 | Rows moving between sections without a drag | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | pinned, unpinned or moved by key or menu: the row travels with the standard spring while the room it leaves and the room it takes close and open with it; to a place out of sight or another Space it collapses out in place and the list does not scroll; ⌘Z plays it back |
| FL-08 | Row buttons (close ×, folder search, reset) | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | ×, audio and folder search buttons: circle fades in on the instant timing; the glyph presses to 0.9 at once and springs back (pop); the click fires on release and the row starts leaving once main has closed the tab, about 2 frames after the release (D70: main decides first, as a pinned tab's × resets it and a page may ask to stay); the reset acts on press (PN-04) |
| FL-09 | Close and archive exit | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | a closing row fades and slides 12 px while its room collapses with the snappy spring and the rows below rise; the next tab is selected no later than the closing row starts to leave, in the first frame after ⌘W at the median of five closes (main wakes a sleeping page only once the change has gone out); the first close after a launch can take 2 frames; a tab whose page the engine lets go first (one that may warn, NV-24) hands over at once too, and shows again only if its page warns (D77 (4)); rows out of sight go without motion |
| FL-10 | Drag and drop: lift, follow, spring, drop | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | a 4 px move lifts the row (1.03, shadow, 95 %) in that frame; the row is drawn under the pointer in every frame; Escape springs it back to its slot |
| FL-11 | Clear Today: staggered sweep | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | Clear sweeps the rows out one after another (25 ms apart, at most 12 staggered) within 450 ms; the divider and New Tab stay; ⌘Z brings them back in one group |
| FL-12 | Folder and pinned-section expand/collapse | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | folders and the pinned section: the chevron turns in 160 ms; the box grows with the snappy spring while its rows fade in 12 ms apart (only when the user opens it); closing is quicker; reduced motion fades |
| FL-13 | Space switching: swipe physics, settle and rubber-band | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | strip of pages, 1:1 tracking, commit thresholds, settle/rubber-band springs, one-page slides for clicks and keys, reduced motion cross-fade; the rubber band keeps the spring FL-13 names (response 0.3 s, ratio 1.0) and comes back within 0.5 px about 480 ms after the last event: FL-29's 350 ms is for swipes that land on a Space (D70) |
| FL-14 | Theme-colour transition between Spaces | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | theme blends with the gesture/spring in OKLab; 200 ms preset blends; light/dark cross-fade |
| FL-15 | Button press micro-animations | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | every icon button presses to 0.94 at once and springs back (pop), the Library button too; Back/Forward nudge, Reload's glyph turns once, the + scales to 0.92; restarts on repeat; none when disabled; no spring with reduced motion |
| FL-16 | Command bar open and close | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | ✅ | motion spring (0.97→1, 4 px drop), 100 ms exit (80 ms after choosing a row) while focus returns at once; fade only with reduced motion; centred in the window |
| FL-17 | Command bar typing and result updates | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | per-keystroke local results, identity-keyed memoized rows, instant highlight; engine suggestions fill free rows without moving the highlight |
| FL-18 | Split view create and resize | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | a tab dragged over the page: the zone shows in the frame after the move that finds it, fades in over 100 ms on the half the new pane takes and moves between halves at once; the new pane grows in from its side with the standard spring and stops in place, without overshoot; the divider follows the pointer 1:1; flip and close travel with the spring (docs/FEEL.md); a tab dragged onto another tab row highlights the half (SV-05) but has no bubble preview or wobble on drop |
| FL-19 | Link preview open, expand, close | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | open: a spring tuned to FL-19's 280–320 ms (response 0.275 s, ratio 0.92; the standard token FL-19 names takes longer over a card's travel, D70), within 2 px in ~320 ms with no overshoot, 18% dim; the page view never resizes or moves with the card (PK-06); expand meets the frame in ~250 ms, then the row enters; split slides to the right half; close 160 ms to 0.96 + fade, the page behind takes clicks again 173–194 ms after Escape (best of up to three rounds, at the edge of 200 ms); drag/swipe dismiss; ⌘Z/⌘⇧T replay the open |
| FL-20 | Favorites tiles | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | a new Favorite pops in from 0.85 with the pop spring while the other tiles re-flow with the snappy spring; a removed one shrinks to 0.85 and fades where it was while the grid closes up |
| FL-21 | Sidebar scrolling and large-sidebar performance | P0 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | only the rows near the visible band are drawn, and every row tells screen readers its place and its list's size, drawn or not; a Space shown for the first time draws a stand-in at once and its list within ~160 ms; on this machine under load a 200-tab fling and a 500-tab scroll still have a few frames of two intervals (5 and 12), so p99 is two intervals, against none over one (docs/FEEL.md) |
| FL-22 | Toasts | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | rise 12 px from 0.96 with the pop spring, at most three 8 px apart, a new one pushes the others up with the snappy spring, stays 3 s (4 s with a button), a hovered one with a button waits until 1 s after the pointer leaves; fade and 8 px drop in 160 ms; under reduced motion a toast fades in where it rests, at its size, and the older ones move at once. In the Space theme; while the sidebar is hidden they show over the bottom centre of the page card (the pane in use in a split), take the pointer and, with a button, are clickable as a whole (SB-13, tabs lane); with the sidebar shown they still show at its foot, not over the page card, and plain ones let clicks through |
| FL-23 | Page loading indicator | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | after 150 ms, a 48x4 theme-accent pill sweeping on a 1.2 s cycle (a pulse with reduced motion); on load end it fills (80 ms) and fades (150 ms), gone 180 ms after; never moves page content |
| FL-24 | Library and Archive motion | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Library opens with a 220 ms fade and 0.98→1 scale (opacity only with reduced motion) and fades out; sections cross-fade in 90 ms; search answers within 50 ms; restored rows fade and the rows below rise; long lists virtualised; a previewed entry opens and closes with the Peek's motion (FL-19) |
| FL-25 | Menus, popovers and tooltips | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | folder search and icon picker: drawn in the first frame, from 0.97 with the snappy timing (150 ms); close with the quick fade; keys go back to the sidebar at once |
| FL-26 | Recent-tab switcher (Ctrl+Tab) | P1 | – | ✅ e2e | – |  |
| FL-27 | Window-level motion | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | a resized window keeps the card's margin in every frame and the page view gets each width within a frame at the median (18 ms at worst), over the page's own colour; the OS full-screen transition; new windows open a step down and right (NV-10) with the command bar's entrance; an inactive window's sidebar dims over 150 ms and comes back at once on focus; no launch sheen (optional) |
| FL-28 | Reduced motion | P0 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | follows the OS setting, with a setting to force it on (AP-17); springs, slides and scales become short fades or instant changes, toasts included, also for what is already on screen when it turns on; a unit guard checks that every motion component sits under the config or reads the setting, and that every element with a layout animation, an entrance, an exit, a press or a moving animate asks useReducedMotion(), since motion reads the config only as an element mounts; drags still follow the pointer and settle with a short ease |

The rubber band comes back in ~480 ms on FL-13's own spring: the 350 ms settle is for swipes that land on a Space (D70) |

## Site customizations

Spec: `spec/boosts.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| BO-01 | Create a site customization for the current site | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | New Tweak… from the command bar (also "customize", "customization", "site style"), the sidebar's + menu, the site controls panel, a paintbrush in the address field (shown on hover, in the accent colour once the site has a Tweak on) and the tab's menu (Tweak this Site…); none bound to a key. Opens the editor over the page with a new Tweak named after the host; a second one adds a second Tweak. A one-screen intro the first time only. Internal pages, error pages, a Peek and a Mini Window take none: the entries are greyed or gone, or say why. A Mini Window has no Tweak entry of its own; a key given to one there says why in the browser window, as a Mini Window shows no notes (with no browser window open, nothing shows). Nothing reloads |
| BO-02 | Editor panel: layout, live preview, close | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | a small view of its own over the page's top-right corner, sized to the panel, draggable by its title and kept inside the page; the page around it stays live. Every change to the look shows at once, while the page is still loading too, and is saved (JavaScript runs with BO-11's Run Now, or the next load); Esc, the close button and Done close it and give the page the keyboard back; the site controls' › and Edit Tweak reopen it as it was. Another page of the site keeps it open; another site or tab closes it; it steps aside for a Peek or full screen. No request names the site. Top to bottom: the name and its ▾ menu (BO-12), the colour area (BO-03 to BO-06), fonts (BO-07), size (BO-08), text case (BO-09), Hide elements (BO-10), the code area (BO-11, which widens the panel to the left), "Also apply to subdomains" (BO-17) and Done. Dragging the wheel recolours the page as fast as the page could itself (BO-03 has the numbers) |
| BO-03 | Colour wheel (theme tint) | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | a wheel with two linked handles: the big one anywhere inside (its angle the hue, its distance how strong), the small one on the rim (the accent: it turns the page's own colours by its distance from the main hue, and turns with the big one). One filter on the page root tints it: white becomes a light tint of the hue, black stays black, text keeps its contrast; images and video keep their colours (an inverse filter), the top layer is tinted too. Arrow keys move the focused handle (⇧ further). Measured with the frame sampler against the page changing the same colours itself, one a frame: the drag keeps up, and main takes an edit for every move (60 of 60, one a frame; an editor that took every other move fails). Under a virtual display with no GPU, 60 a second at 1024×768 (slowest frame 17 ms); at 1440×900 the page itself manages only about 35 a second there, and the drag matches it |
| BO-04 | Invert lightness ("make this site dark") | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the lightbulb next to the wheel inverts lightness and keeps hues (white page dark, text light), with the tint on the inverted result; photos and video keep their own look; again restores it |
| BO-05 | Advanced colour sliders | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the sliders button opens Contrast, Brightness and Original saturation, live as they move; each has a marked neutral middle (100%) that changes nothing, and a double-click puts it back there |
| BO-06 | Reset colours | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the circle-with-a-cross button puts the wheel, invert and sliders back to neutral, so the page shows its own colours; fonts, size, case, hidden elements and code stay |
| BO-07 | Font override presets | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | eight "Aa" presets, each in its own typeface: Sans, Serif, Classic, Humanist, Rounded, Mono, Typewriter and Hand. One applies to all the site's text but icon fonts, glyphs hidden from screen readers, code and math; the active one again gives the site its fonts back. The presets are font stacks of what the system has, so nothing is bundled and their look varies by system (Rounded and Hand fall back on Linux); shipping freely licensed fonts is open |
| BO-08 | Page size (zoom) control | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | − and + step the page through 90, 100, 110, 125 and 150%, saved with the Tweak, so every visit gets it; it multiplies with the tab's own zoom (⌘+ / ⌘−) and leaves that alone |
| BO-09 | Text case control | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | one button cycles As written, lowercase, UPPERCASE, Capitalized Words and back; fields, editable text and code keep their own case |
| BO-10 | Hide-element mode | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the lightning button: the element under the pointer gets an outline with its kind and size, and the page's links and buttons don't act: the picker stops each click and press on its way to them, except the page's own listeners on its window, which can still hear them first; and if the page takes the picker's layer away, the layer comes back (a page that keeps taking it ends the mode); a click picks. The panel then offers Hide this, or Hide all similar with a slider from narrow to broad, counting what it would hide, and how many of those show now where some don't ("5 (4 shown)"), and outlining those in the page. Gone at once and saved as plain CSS selectors, so hidden from the first frame on every page of the site where it matches. Done or Esc leaves the mode (Esc drops a pick first); another document ends it. On a page still loading, the mode starts when the load ends: a click on the button shows it starting at once, the button pressed and the panel saying it starts when the page has loaded, and the page acts as usual until then; Done or Esc, in the panel or the page, cancels the start (the page still gets its Esc), and another document ends it. The picker runs in an isolated world, never the page's own. Each hide has a restore marker in the panel (not over the page's corner): hovered it shows the element again, clicked it brings it back |
| BO-11 | Code editor: custom CSS and JavaScript per site | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the { } button opens a code area with CSS and JavaScript tabs, empty to start. CSS applies as it is typed (about 90 ms from the keystroke to the page's frame, measured) and is saved as typed, sent before the panel closes; a reload keeps it. JavaScript runs in the page's own world once per load at document ready, from main; Run now runs it at once, Reload page loads the page again. The editor: monospace, syntax colouring (text only, never markup), line numbers, the platform's undo (⌘Z / Ctrl+Z through Orbit's key handling), Tab and ⇧Tab indent and outdent, Enter keeps the indentation. Errors, thrown or syntax, go to the page's console; no dialog, nothing in main. JavaScript from elsewhere stays off until Allow on this device, and editing it doesn't allow it. A JS badge in the site controls list and the code tab (the Library's list comes with BO-15) |
| BO-12 | Name, rename and reset all edits | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the title is the Tweak's name with a ▾ menu: Rename… edits it in place (Enter keeps, Esc cancels), Reset all edits… asks first, then clears colours, font, size, case, hidden elements and code; the name and switches stay. The menu works from the keyboard; Esc closes it, not the panel |
| BO-13 | Shuffle (random style) | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Shuffle in the name ▾ menu applies a random look live: any hue at a moderate strength, an accent a pleasing step away, sometimes inverted, one of the fonts, the site's size or a little larger, mostly the site's case. The menu stays open to shuffle again; hidden elements and code are never touched |
| BO-14 | Enable / disable a customization (per site) | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the site controls panel lists the site's Tweaks by name with a paintbrush, coloured when on and grey when off; the name turns one off or on at once, without a reload, while the page is still loading too, each on its own, keeping all its settings; the › opens it in the editor. The address field's paintbrush shows in the accent colour while one is on and grey when all are off, and turns them all off or on. Off, a Tweak's styles leave the page at once; what its JavaScript already did stays until the page loads again |
| BO-15 | Manage all customizations (list view in the Library) | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the Library's Tweaks section lists every Tweak on this device by site, a site's oldest first: its name, its site (where the name doesn't say it, and "and its subdomains"), a JS badge where it has JavaScript (struck through where that isn't allowed on this device) and a switch that turns it off or on at once. Right-click or ⋯ (the Library's own menu): Edit shows the site's tab in the Space (never a Peek's or a Mini Window's page), or opens the site, and opens the editor once the page can take it; a site that doesn't load stops the wait as its load fails, with a note saying so; Open Site shows that tab, else opens a new tab where the Tweak was made (scheme, host and port); Rename… in place; Delete… asks first, and its styles leave open pages at once (its JavaScript's effects with their next load). Keys: up and down, Enter edits, Space switches, F2 renames, Delete asks, Shift+F10 opens the menu. The command bar's View Tweaks opens it. With none, a short explanation and Tweak This Site for the page underneath |
| BO-16 | Global on/off switch for all customizations | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Settings → Advanced: "Apply Tweaks on websites I visit", on by default. Off, every open page loses its Tweaks' styles at once, while still loading too, and the editor closes; what a Tweak's JavaScript already did stays until the page loads again, as the setting says; the address field's paintbrush and the + menu's and the tab menu's New Tweak go; the command bar's says Tweaks are off; the site controls panel and the Library say so, the Library with Turn On. Each Tweak keeps its own on or off for when they are back on. The organisation policy is P2 and not built |
| BO-17 | Scope: which pages a customization applies to | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | a Tweak is for its host's pages: any path, query and in-page navigation, not another host, the parent domain or a subdomain. "Also apply to subdomains" (off by default, at the panel's foot) brings in subdomains' open pages at once; it isn't offered for an address by number and is fixed while the page is on a subdomain it brings in. Every profile gets the same Tweaks; in a private window the CSS applies and the JavaScript runs only once "Also run in private windows" is ticked. Matching is a map lookup per label of the host |
| BO-18 | How customizations apply on page load (timing, safety) | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the page preload asks main for the site's sheets before the page's first paint (D40) and puts them in as injected sheets (D85), which the page can't read or remove, and which its own layered !important rules can't outrank: no frame shows the page without its Tweak (frame-capture tests on a slow page's hard reload and first visit, on a page that sets its own adopted sheets in its head, and on one with a layered !important background). Main puts in its own copies at document ready, or at the first change before it, then tells the preload to take its copies out, by a message that carries only the document's number and that main never waits for. Survives reloads, back and forward, a reopened tab, a woken tab and a restart. JavaScript runs from main once per load at document ready, main frame only, where allowed (BO-11, BO-17), and checks the page's host itself as it runs: not again on an in-page navigation, never in a frame from another site; what it did stays until the next load. The Space colours come with BO-19 |
| BO-19 | Use Space theme colours inside customization CSS | P2 | – | ✅ unit | – |  |
| BO-20 | Sharing customizations and the customization gallery | P2 | – | ✅ e2e | – |  |
| BO-21 | Customization commands in the command bar | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | in the command bar, none bound to a key: New Tweak… (also "customize", "customization", "site style"), Edit Tweak (the site's one in the editor; with several, the site controls list them to pick from; with none, a note says so), Turn Off and Turn On Tweaks for This Site (with a note), View Tweaks (the Library's list, BO-15). In a Mini Window, View Tweaks opens the Library in the browser window (one that isn't private), and the others say there why its page takes no Tweak; from a Mini Window with no browser window open, they show nothing. Export Tweak… comes with BO-20 |
| BO-22 | Legacy code-only customization builder | OOS | ⛔ out of scope | – | – | the spec leaves it out |

A key held down acts once. Copy, paste (after DevTools' own paste warning) and the device toolbar work; links DevTools open become tabs. Windows/Linux: while DevTools have the keyboard, only the DevTools keys reach Orbit |

Picker: ⌥⌘C on macOS, no default key on Windows/Linux, Inspect Element in the command bar. ⇧⌘C stays Copy URL; inside DevTools it is DevTools' own picker. Remap: give the devtools.inspect action ⇧⌘C (and take it from tab.copyUrl) in src/shared/actions.ts, or in Settings → Shortcuts once remapping (ST-08) lands |

Undocked: the open key brings them to the front (checked on Linux; macOS unverified), and closes them when they have the keyboard. No windows added, however many tabs have DevTools. What Orbit puts over a page (find bar, zoom, link pill, loading indicator, permission prompt) goes over the page's own area, never over docked DevTools (e2e for the find bar and link pill, docked right, bottom and left) |

Only the page's own address goes, so a web page can't make Orbit open a file: URL this way (D49) |

They follow the app's state (light/dark) through the same bridge as Orbit's UI, which the one web page preload (src/preload/page.ts) gives an orbit: page's main frame only (D40, D53). A web page can't navigate, frame, redirect to, open, load or fetch them, and gets no bridge: Orbit opens one for no page but another internal page on any route (the page menu, Split View's item included, ⌥-click, new tabs, windows and pop-ups, a pop-up's own, blocked pop-ups, a drop), D53. Each page runs only the commands listed for it and sends no events, and its document runs only its own scripts (script-src 'self'), D53. Infrastructure documented for reuse (D39) in src/main/devtools/internal-pages.ts and src/renderer/src/internal/registry.ts: a page is a *.internal-page.tsx module, and lists the commands it runs in INTERNAL_PAGE_COMMANDS. Missing: the pages other lanes add as they build them (D54): extensions EX-07, site settings OT-07/ST-13, privacy and clearing data and system options ST-12, languages ST-14, about UP-07; orbit://pages/ lists each one added |

A crashed page hands the keyboard to the window, so ⇧⌘R brings it back. Stopping a load (Esc in the page, double-clicking Reload) is NV-04, built with the sidebar's Reload/Stop button; its e2e tests cover both |

Programs, installers, scripts and disk images wait under their partial name with Keep / Discard in the sidebar row, the Library and the flyout, through a restart too: everywhere exe, msi, dmg, pkg, deb, rpm, AppImage, .desktop launchers, sh/bash/zsh/py/pl/rb scripts, iso/img/vhd/vhdx, jar, jnlp, apk…; on Windows also its own script, shortcut and system types (js, vbs, wsf, hta, lnk, url, scf, settingcontent-ms, chm, reg, inf, msc, dll…). Keep puts the file in place and marks it, Discard deletes it. Every such file is held, whatever the site, as there is no reputation service. Gap, by the spec's own rule (D54): Safe Browsing, which needs a reputation service; none is free to use (Google's is non-commercial, Web Risk is paid) |

On Windows, Orbit can be the app for local .pdf files (P2): the installer registers it (win.fileAssociations, class Orbit.PDF), Settings → General → Open PDFs with Orbit sends the user to Windows' Default apps (only the user can choose there) and says when Orbit is the one, and a file Windows passes on the command line opens in a tab, as macOS's open-file does; unverified on Windows (no Windows build is tested; e2e stands in for it) |
| DL-14 | Downloads keyboard shortcut and menu | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | Windows/Linux: Ctrl+J opens the downloads flyout at the top left, beside the sidebar (Orbit has no top toolbar): the 12 newest with live progress, Keep/Discard, Resume/Retry/Cancel and Show in Folder; a click opens a file, rows drag out (DL-06), Show All opens the Library's Downloads section; Esc, Ctrl+J again or a click outside closes it. macOS: ⌘⇧J and ⌥⌘L open the Library's Downloads section (KS-12). The command bar has a "Downloads" action |
| DL-15 | Pause, resume and retry | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | Pause/Resume from the row's menu (and a Resume button on a paused row); a cut-off download shows Resume when the server sent an ETag or Last-Modified (continues with a range request), else Retry (starts again); one cut off by quitting resumes after a restart from its partial file (kept under a hidden second name while the engine shuts down). Downloads never block the tab that started them |
| DL-16 | Downloads in private windows, Little windows and Peek | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | Peek and Mini Window downloads go to the same list as any other. A private window's downloads save to disk like any other but are in no saved list (not the downloads list, nor the state file or its backup), and their Windows Zone.Identifier names no address. A private window shows only its own session's downloads (sidebar row, Ctrl+J flyout), and no other window shows them; their start, toasts and the files Orbit opens stay in its windows, and they change nothing kept (the Library's section, the Dock's notification names no file). They stay listed while a private window is open, its pages closed or not; when the last one closes (the session ends), they leave every list: finished files stay on disk, one still coming is saved and then leaves, a paused or stopped one and a program held back (DL-12) are discarded. Tested with real private windows |
| DL-17 | Dock / taskbar progress | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | ✅ | While downloads run or are paused, their overall progress shows on the macOS Dock icon and on the windows' taskbar buttons: bytes received of those with a known size, the can't-tell bar when no size is known, Windows' paused colour when every one is paused; it goes when none runs. A download that finishes while no Orbit window has focus bounces the Dock icon once (macOS) and shows a "Download complete" notification naming the file (a private window's isn't named). Tests read what Orbit asks of the OS through test hooks; the OS's own drawing isn't checked on Linux |
| DL-18 | Smart renaming of downloads | OOS | ⛔ out of scope | – | – | the spec leaves it out |

Files are read in a worker, in time linear in their size (D58): main’s longest stall is about 0.07 s for a 16 MB file or list, and about 0.2 s for a 60 MB file of 200,000 bookmarks. A file nested deeper than 64 folders keeps its deeper bookmarks in the 64th; a file gives at most 200,000 bookmarks (folders don’t count) and 20,000 folders, the bookmarks of folders past that kept in the folder that holds them; over 64 MB, every route, a paste included, says “This is too large to import (the limit is 64 MB)” without reading it; a read that fails says “Orbit couldn’t read this file”. No passwords CSV (D52) |

Bookmarks are made out of sight, in parts, and their folder is shown whole, at once (D62): while 20,000 are added, the browser window’s longest freeze is under 0.1 s; 100,000 take about 34 s, with the window’s longest freeze about 0.34 s and main’s longest stall about 0.57 s (saving the state). Until the folder shows, nothing lists its tabs (D65): not the command bar (by title, by address or among recent tabs), the recent-tab switcher or the Library. One the user reached anyway and placed stays where they put it, and the folder leaves it out. Restore Data part-way stops the import first: its tabs are removed without going to the Archive, and the import window says “The import stopped: data was restored from a backup.” Copies of the other browser’s files go in a folder under Orbit’s user data, removed at quit (a copy still being made too) and cleared at startup (D58) |

Orbit's own pages and private windows' profiles are left out. Copy All Links on a folder is the tabs lane's (it exists) |

| OB-09 | Done screen and the first browser window | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Done screen sums up colours, Favorites, ad blocking, default browser and import (what will be added from where, e.g. "6 bookmarks from bookmarks.html", or that nothing was and where import lives); Start browsing opens the first window centred at 80% of the screen (its work area), with the colours and Favorites picked and the command bar closed. Its pinned section starts with an open "Orbit basics" folder (Getting Started and Orbit Help, unloaded until opened; an import's folder, collapsed if large (IM-05), goes below it), and its one Today tab, in front, is orbit://welcome/: five tips with the keys as they are now, and links to the guide, Help and the shortcut sheet. Skip setup gets the same first window; Back to browsing after a reset returns to the open window and adds nothing. The card is OB-16 (P2) |
| OB-10 | Getting-started guide | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Getting Started (command bar, also found as "guide" or "tutorial"; the macOS Help menu; the Orbit basics folder; links on Help and the welcome tab) opens orbit://guide/, a page that comes with Orbit and works offline: the sidebar, Spaces, Today and the Archive, pinned tabs and Favorites, the command bar, split view, Peek, the Mini Window and site controls, each with its keys as they are now (KS-18: a remap shows at once). It ends with the essential shortcuts as a table (OB-12's groups), a button for the shortcut sheet and a link to Settings → Shortcuts. The Orbit basics folder takes the place of a Space of its own |
| OB-11 | Contextual tips and one-time hints | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Tooltips name the keys: "New Tab (⌘T)", the tab in front's Close and Mute, the pinned caret and the window's Close (when it has a key), as the toolbar, Library and Space buttons already did; they follow remaps (KS-18). Hints are toasts with a ✕ that stay 6 s, longer while hovered, no wider than the sidebar (over the page's corner while it is hidden), and never block the page: the first time Today tabs are archived on their own, once, how many, after how long and how to restore them, with View Archive (shown once a browser window is in front, so tabs archived at launch are explained when the user looks); a hidden sidebar, three times, its key and the left edge, with Show. Esc anywhere in the window dismisses them and still reaches the page; counts are kept in the state file, and Reset Onboarding keeps them. Toasts for what happens out of view were there already and stay as SB-13 and FL-22 set them (3–4 s, every time): "Opened in a new tab" + Show with the sidebar hidden, and "Restored to <Space>" + Go to Space (AR-05) |
| OB-12 | Essential keyboard shortcuts sheet | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Help → Keyboard Shortcuts (macOS Help menu; the command bar’s Keyboard Shortcuts everywhere; a key can be assigned) opens a sheet over the window with the essential keys as they are now (KS-18), grouped Everyday, Navigation, Spaces and Split View, “None” for an action with no key; Esc, ✕, a click outside, Close Tab’s keys or asking again close it; the link at the bottom opens Settings → Shortcuts. Asked from Settings or a Mini Window, it opens over the browser window behind (a new one if there is none) |
| OB-13 | Help and feedback entry points | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Help (command bar, F1 on Windows and Linux, the macOS Help menu) opens orbit://help/, Orbit's own page, which works offline: the guide, answers (where tabs went, with View Archive and Reopen Closed Tab's key; where the sidebar went; import; privacy; updates), the shortcut sheet and Settings → Shortcuts, Report a Bug and Copy Build Info. Report a Bug (there, in the command bar and in the Help menu) opens a new issue on the project's tracker with the build info filled in: a draft the user reads and sends. The macOS Help menu also has Getting Started and Keyboard Shortcuts (OB-10, OB-12). The help pages can run only those few actions and open Settings |
| OB-14 | Skip, resume and reset onboarding | P2 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | Skip setup on every step but the last gives the spec's default first window: the theme step's colours and mode are undone, no Favorites are added and the ads step's choice isn't applied (D44). The step, the theme, the Favorites and the ads choice picked so far are saved, so a quit part-way resumes there with them. An import chosen at the import step isn’t: it waits in memory for Start browsing, so a quit before then loses it, and the Done step says nothing was imported (it’s in Settings, under General); Reset Onboarding (command bar only) runs the flow again over the open windows and deletes nothing |

## Updates (delivery and surfacing)

Spec: `spec/updates.md`

| ID | Feature | P | Built | Tested | Feels right | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| UP-01 | Background update checks | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | checks a release feed at launch (after 30 s) and about every 4 h ± 30 min, after wake if overdue; silent, failures retried at the next check; a private in-memory session that sends only Orbit's version, system and processor type (no cookies). A newer release with a file for this system (Orbit's feed: files["linux-x64"…] with url, SHA-256 and size; GitHub: an asset named …-<system>.tar.gz/.zip/.exe with its digest) downloads in the background into the user's data folder, checked against its size and SHA-256 (a mismatch is deleted), and is unpacked beside Orbit (Linux folder build: .tar.gz; macOS: .zip of Orbit.app; Windows: the installer, run silently at the relaunch); only then does anything show (UP-02). A copy that can't replace itself (development run, AppImage/Snap/Flatpak, a folder it can't write, a Mac copy run from where it was downloaded, a Windows copy its installer didn't put in place) gets UP-10's page instead. Nothing is checked until a feed is set in Settings → General: empty by default, as nothing is published yet; test and dev builds accept only a feed on this computer and follow no redirect. macOS and Windows installs unverified (no build of theirs is tested) |
| UP-02 | "Update ready" banner in the sidebar → relaunch | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e | – | sidebar banner above the Space switcher, in the Space's colours, once the update has downloaded: the pill "Update ready" ("Important security update" for a security fix, UP-12) opens on hover to the release's line and a gradient "Relaunch to update"; one click relaunches into it (UP-05). Downloads in progress ask first (DL-01's question), then each page with unsaved changes ("Leave site?", NV-24); Cancel keeps Orbit as it was. ✕ hides it for 24 h or until the next launch. An update Orbit can't install itself shows UP-10's "New version available" |
| UP-03 | Manual "Check for updates…" | P1 | 🟡 partial | ✅ e2e | – | command bar and macOS app menu "Check for Updates…" open Settings → About (not a separate window) and check: Checking…, up to date, the failure, or the new version with Download → its progress (a bar and a percentage) → Relaunch, two clicks, when automatic checks are off (on, it downloads by itself and Settings shows the progress, then Relaunch); where Orbit can't install it, Download opens the release page (UP-10); a failed download says why, and Download asks the feed again; a click on the version copies it. Not built: the Turn on offer (UP-04, P2), a ☰ entry on Windows/Linux (SB-26's app menu, P2, not built) |
| UP-04 | Automatic installation while idle (opt-in) | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| UP-05 | Relaunch behaviour | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | the relaunch closes the windows (on macOS and Windows they fade out in about 190 ms, none with reduced motion; Linux can't fade a window: Electron's setOpacity is macOS/Windows only), quits, puts the update in place and starts Orbit again; windows, Spaces, tabs and split views come back from the state file (TB-22), each page at its place, scroll and form text with Back and Forward (ST-16), and only the shown tabs load. e2e (a test run installs nothing and is started again as the new version): quit 165 ms, start 1.7 s at load 6.5 |
| UP-06 | "What's new" after an update and release notes in-app | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | after a version change the sidebar shows "Updated to Orbit X" with the release's one line (the line the feed gave the update Orbit installed, or the feed's line for this version when it was installed otherwise) and See what's new, which opens that release's page (else its GitHub release notes) in a tab; ends when opened, dismissed or after 3 days; command bar "What's New" and Help → Release Notes |
| UP-07 | About window and version info | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | About Orbit (app menu) opens Settings → About: logo, version, engine, Electron, build date (set at build time), Copy build info, and the licence and open-source credits from a page that comes with the app (D43); Help → Troubleshooting → Copy Build Info and the command-bar action copy version, build date, engine, OS and processor |
| UP-08 | Beta update channel | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| UP-09 | OS support notices | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| UP-10 | Orbit update stub (unsigned builds) | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | reads Orbit's JSON feed ({version, url, summary, security, files}) or a GitHub releases API answer (latest, or a list: newest non-draft, non-pre-release); a newer version Orbit can't install itself (no file for this system, or a copy that can't replace itself, UP-01) shows "New version available" and opens its page in a tab; one it can install downloads and relaunches (UP-01, UP-02). No feed is set up yet: the address is empty by default. The pill opens on hover or keyboard focus only: after a click it closes once the pointer leaves (sign-off 3) |
| UP-11 | Update failure handling | P2 | – | – | – |  |
| UP-12 | Engine security updates cadence | P1 | ✅ | ✅ e2e+unit | – | a release marked [security] in its GitHub name or notes, or security: true in Orbit's feed, shows "Important security update" in the banner and Settings. The whole title shows at any sidebar width (180 to 420 px): it wraps rather than being cut, with the ✕'s room kept on its first line only; "Relaunch to update" wraps too at the narrowest (sign-off 3) |
